From an overflow to beach risk (S3–S4)

S2 says how likely each basin is to overflow today. S3 decides which of the basin's beaches an overflow reaches (the beach split), and S4 how long it keeps them over standard (the lingering table), from how long beaches actually stayed dirty after real overflows. Together they turn today's and the past week's overflow chances into the chance a beach group is fouled today. This page opens S3 and S4 up for the live forecast and every other model set: what every set shares, what differs, and a walk-through of any day in the hindcast.

The transformation

For a beach group on day D, take today's and each of the previous seven days' discharge probability for the group's basin (S2). With a split (S3), first multiply each by the share of the basin's overflows that reach the group. Multiply each by the lingering fraction x(k, size) from S4's table: the share of sample days that were over standard k days after a discharge of that size, with the dry-weather background removed. Each product is "the chance that day's discharge is fouling the beach today". Assume independence, multiply the chances that each one is not, and take one minus the product. A discharge day itself is a stay-out day by rule, so x(0) = 1 and the group risk on a discharge day is never below the group's probability.

riskgroup(D) = 1 − ∏k=0..7 ( 1 − pgroup(D−k) · x(k, size(D−k)) ) x(0, ·) = 1 pgroup(D) = pbasin(D) · [w · glarge + (1 − w) · gsmall] S3, the split: g = the group's share of the basin's overflow days (no split: pgroup = pbasin) x(k, size) = (ptable(k, size) − baseline) / (1 − baseline) S4, the lingering table: attributable P(elevated), background removed size = predicted discharge volume V (MG) from the basin's volume head → blend weight w = V / (V + median event) x(k, V) = w · xlarge(k) + (1 − w) · xsmall(k) riskzone(D) = max over the zone's groups

What every set shares, and what differs

Every model set, the live forecast and each candidate, runs through the same composition code with the same volume heads. What differs is what S2 feeds in (the daily probabilities, and the rain source each basin model reads) and, for a set without Outfall split, S3 and S4: No split and Linger table 1. The volume heads read the rain source they were trained on, whichever S2 is in play.

S3 · Outfall split

stored as stage 2 v2

S2 predicts one probability per basin, but a basin's outfalls post different beaches: on the Westside, three outfalls post Ocean Beach and four post Baker and China Beach; in North Shore, four post Crissy Field and three post Aquatic Park. With No split (stored as stage 2 v1), both groups get the basin's whole probability, so a Sea Cliff discharge turns Ocean Beach red. Outfall split multiplies the basin probability by the share of that basin's CIWQS discharge days, by size class, on which at least one of the group's own outfalls discharged, and S4's lingering table is refit on those group-attributed days (Linger table 2). Where a group's outfalls are the whole basin (Mission Creek, Southeast) the share is 1 and nothing changes.

S4 · The lingering tables

Linger table 1 was fitted once, with Trees (2026-09-12), from every sample day within a week of a CIWQS discharge: for each beach group, size class and days-since bucket, the share of sample days over standard, with the count behind it. Linger table 2 is the same fit on group-attributed days, with S3's Outfall split. Serving smooths each small/large curve to be non-increasing over days (weighted pool-adjacent-violators), because contamination decays and cells with 3–6 samples are noisy enough to read day 3 above day 1.

Cells: P(elevated) with n underneath; hover for the attributable value. Curves: attributable x(k) — solid large, dashed small, orange dots the blend at the chosen volume.

S2 · Volume heads: the size S3 and S4 read

A gradient-boosted regressor per basin predicts log(1 + MG) from the same 19 rain features, trained only on events with a reported volume. Its only job in S3 and S4 is the blend weight w = V / (V + median event), which saturates fast: above a few times the median, every discharge is "large". Self-check: this page vs the stored artifacts

For every model set and every group, the page recomposes the group risk on every day of the hindcast from the exported S2 probabilities and shared volumes, and compares with the risk stored in that set's scorecard artifact (3 decimals). This is the same arithmetic the Model check page's numbers rest on.
